blocks.html: Robinsons Land Corporation has opened work.able Iloilo, the biggest flexible workspace in Western Visayas, designed for today’s growing companies, startups, creatives, small teams, freelancers, and even students.

Located on the 10th floor of Cybergate Iloilo Tower 3 in Pavia, work.able Iloilo gives users a ready-to-use space to get things done, collaborate, explore creative pursuits, and stay productive in one of the country’s fastest-growing business and lifestyle destinations. The center sits beside Robinsons Pavia Mall, giving members easy access to dining, retail, errands, and everyday essentials between work sessions.

Accessibility is also part of the appeal. Located beside a major transport terminal, the center connects users to bus and jeepney routes across Iloilo and nearby areas, making it easier to drop in for a full workday, a few productive hours, or a meeting with classmates, clients, or collaborators.

“Spaces matter because they shape how people work, communicate, and build opportunities,” said Jericho P. Go, Senior Vice President and Business Unit General Manager of Robinsons Offices, which serves as the landlord of work.able Iloilo. With work.able Iloilo, Robinsons Offices is providing a well-located, thoughtfully designed environment that gives Iloilo a new setting for ideas, collaboration, and everyday productivity.”

The interiors bring together modern office design and a distinctly Ilonggo character. Inspired by the energy and artistry of the Dinagyang Festival, work.able Iloilo features rhythmic textures, layered details, bold accents, warm wood tones, earthy palettes, and locally sourced materials. A neon-lit “Maayong Aga” welcomes guests into a setting that feels polished, familiar, and proudly Filipino, whether they are settling in for a productive session, casual meetups, quick selfies, or their next TikTok.

The center is built to support different work styles throughout the day. It offers reliable, high-speed WiFi for virtual meetings, content creation, online classes, and daily tasks, along with complimentary coffee and high-end espresso machines for latte-style drinks.

Users can choose from plug-and-play coworking seats, 25 private offices with over 420 workstations, boardrooms, meeting rooms, focus pods, phone booths, a common pantry, and a town hall that can accommodate up to 90 people in a dining setup and up to 185 guests in a training or town hall configuration. Added support spaces include a dedicated clinic with a treatment bed and a private lactation room for breastfeeding mothers.

“work.able Iloilo was designed to make work feel easier, more flexible, and more connected,” said Elton John Peralta, Senior Director and Head of work.able. “Whether someone needs a quiet desk, a meeting room, a private office, or a place to build ideas, the space gives users the freedom to choose how they want to work.”
To give more people a chance to try the space, work.able Iloilo is offering a limited-time welcome experience until July 31, 2026, where guests can enjoy a free hot desk seat and
experience the space firsthand. Coworking access is available Mondays to Fridays from 8 a.m. to 6 p.m., while private offices are available 24/7 for those who need extended work hours.
For inquiries, visit workable.ph, follow @workableph on Facebook and Instagram, or email enablers@workable.ph.

blocks.cap: (L-R) Mr. Jericho P. Go, SVP and Business Unit General Manager of Robinsons Offices and work.able landlord, together with Mr. Elton John N. Peralta, Senior Director and Head of work.able, marks the opening of work.able Iloilo with a ceremonial ribbon cutting.
Blending comfort and functionality, work.able Iloilo’s co-working space provides a modern setting where ideas flow, and professionals can work, connect, and grow.

A vibrant Dinagyang dance performance energizes the launch of work.able Iloilo, bringing the spirit of the iconic festival to life and celebrating Iloilo’s rich culture, creativity, and sense of community.

(L-R) Mr. Elton John N. Peralta, Senior Director and Head of work.able, and Mr. Jericho P. Go, SVP and Business Unit General Manager and work.able landlord, pose with the Dinagyang Dancers during the ceremonial opening of work.able Iloilo.
